question: Which of the following is a food-borne disease caused by the consumption of contaminated food or beverages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cholera.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cholera is an acute food-borne and water-borne disease caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, contracted by consuming food or water contaminated with the bacteria. (हैजा — दूषित भोजन/जल से फैलने वाला रोग)

 

• It causes severe watery diarrhoea and dehydration, and can be fatal within hours if untreated. Oral rehydration therapy (ORT) is the mainstay of treatment.

 

• Poor sanitation and unsafe drinking water are the main sources of cholera outbreaks, which is why it is classified as a food/water-borne disease rather than a vector-borne or air-borne one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common food/water-borne diseases include typhoid, hepatitis A, dysentery and diarrhoea.

 

• The WHO classifies diseases by mode of transmission into water-borne, vector-borne, air-borne and contact diseases, among others.

 

NOTE

 

• Malaria (Option 1): A vector-borne disease caused by the *Plasmodium* parasite, transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

 

• Tuberculosis (Option 2): An air-borne disease caused by the bacterium *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, spread through droplets from an infected person's cough or sneeze.

 

• Chicken pox (Option 3): A contagious viral (air-borne/contact) disease caused by the varicella-zoster virus, spread through direct contact or respiratory droplets.

question: Which key can be pressed to initiate a slide show in MS PowerPoint?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Function key F5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pressing F5 in Microsoft PowerPoint starts the slide show from the very first slide. (स्लाइड शो — F5 कुंजी)

 

• Pressing Shift + F5 instead starts the slide show from the current slide rather than from the beginning.

 

• These shortcuts work in the standard desktop version of MS PowerPoint and are among the most commonly tested MS Office shortcut keys.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• F7 is used for Spelling check, and F12 opens the Save As dialog box in PowerPoint/Word.

 

• Esc is used to end/exit a running slide show.

 

NOTE

 

• Function key F4 (Option 1): Repeats the last action performed.

 

• Function key F2 (Option 2): Used to rename a selected object/placeholder text box.

 

• Function key F8 (Option 3): Not a standard slide-show shortcut in PowerPoint.

question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights has been deleted from the original list of fundamental rights provided in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Property, originally guaranteed as a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 of the Constitution, was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. (संपत्ति का अधिकार — 44वां संविधान संशोधन)

 

• It was made a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A, which was newly inserted, stating that no person shall be deprived of their property except by authority of law.

 

• This is the only Fundamental Right originally included in Part III of the Constitution that has since been deleted.

 

• The 44th Amendment was enacted during the Janata Party government (Morarji Desai) to prevent misuse of emergency provisions and to reduce the scope of litigation over property rights that had clashed with land-reform legislation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original Constitution provided 7 Fundamental Rights; after this deletion, only 6 Fundamental Rights remain (Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies).

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Right to freedom of religion (Option 1): Still a Fundamental Right under Articles 25-28.

 

• Cultural and educational rights (Option 2): Still a Fundamental Right under Articles 29-30.

 

• Right to constitutional remedies (Option 3): Still a Fundamental Right under Article 32, and remains in force.

question: The approach driven by seven engines, which is powered by Clean Energy and ‘Sabka Prayas’ is related to which scheme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Gati Shakti Master Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PM GatiShakti National Master Plan was launched on 13 October 2021 to provide multimodal connectivity infrastructure for various economic zones. (पीएम गति शक्ति — सात इंजन)

 

• It is driven by seven engines: Railways, Roads, Ports, Waterways, Airports, Mass Transport and Logistics Infrastructure, complemented by the pillars of Energy Transmission and IT Communication.

 

• The plan is guided by six pillars — Comprehensiveness, Prioritisation, Optimisation, Synchronisation, Analytical and Dynamic — and is powered by Clean Energy and driven by the spirit of ‘Sabka Prayas’ (everyone's effort) for holistic infrastructure development.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM GatiShakti aims to reduce logistics costs in India (as a percentage of GDP) and improve multimodal connectivity across ministries and departments through a common digital platform.

 

• It builds upon and integrates schemes like Bharatmala, Sagarmala, UDAN and industrial corridors.

 

NOTE

 

• Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (Option 1): An employment-generation scheme for the post-COVID recovery period, incentivising new employment.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (Option 2): A scheme providing collateral-free micro-loans to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

 

• Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan (Option 3): A rural public-works/employment scheme launched in 2020 for migrant workers returning during the COVID-19 pandemic.

question: Bilhan was a court poet in which of the following kingdoms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vikramaditya VI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bilhana (Bilhan) was a renowned Kashmiri Sanskrit poet who served as the court poet (*Vidyapati*) of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI of Kalyani. (बिल्हण — विक्रमादित्य षष्ठ)

 

• His most celebrated work is the “Vikramankadevacharita”, a historical *mahakavya* (epic poem) that eulogises the life and reign of Vikramaditya VI.

 

• He is also known for the erotic lyric poem “Chaurapanchasika” ("Fifty Stanzas of a Thief"), traditionally believed to have been composed in the voice of a condemned lover.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Western Chalukyas of Kalyani (also called the Later Chalukyas) ruled the Deccan between the 10th and 12th centuries CE, with Vikramaditya VI being one of their most powerful rulers, known for his long and prosperous reign (the "Chalukya Vikrama Era").

 

• Other notable court poets of medieval India include Kalhana (Rajatarangini, under Kashmiri kings) and Banabhatta (Harshacharita, under Harshavardhana).

 

NOTE

 

• Rajaraja II (Option 2): A Chola king; the poet Ottakoothar was associated with the Chola court.

 

• Vijayaditya VII (Option 3): An Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi, not associated with Bilhana.

 

• Kulottunga I (Option 4): A Chola king under whom the Tamil epic Kalingattupparani was composed by the poet Jayamkondar.

question: Manipur's ____________ tribe celebrates the ‘Gaan-Ngai’ festival, which is a post-harvest festival of the tribe living in the regions of Manipur.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zeliangrong.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gaan-Ngai is the most important post-harvest festival of the Zeliangrong community (a composite name for the Zeme, Liangmei and Rongmei Naga tribes), celebrated across Manipur, Nagaland and Assam. (गान-नगाई पर्व — जेलियांगरोंग जनजाति)

 

• It is celebrated on the 13th day (the 10th lunar day) of the Manipuri month of Wakching (around November-December), marking the end of the year's harvest and worship of the household deity Tingkao Ragwang.

 

• The festival involves community feasting, traditional dances, and rituals performed at both the household and community level over several days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major tribal festivals of Manipur include Lui-Ngai-Ni (seed-sowing festival of the Naga tribes) and Chumpha (festival of the Tangkhul Nagas).

 

• The Zeliangrong Union was formed in the 1930s to unite the Zeme, Liangmei and Rongmei tribes under one cultural and political identity.

 

NOTE

 

• Chothe (Option 2): A Kuki-Chin tribe of Manipur; not associated with Gaan-Ngai.

 

• Gangte (Option 3): Another Kuki-Chin tribe of Manipur, distinct from the Zeliangrong group.

 

• Inpui (Option 4): A smaller Naga tribe of Manipur, related to but distinct from the Zeliangrong grouping that specifically observes Gaan-Ngai.

question: Who among the following confirmed Maxwell's theories with the discovery of radio waves and also became the first person to transmit and receive controlled radio waves in 1886?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heinrich Hertz.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Heinrich Rudolf Hertz, a German physicist, experimentally proved James Clerk Maxwell's electromagnetic theory by being the first person to transmit and receive controlled radio waves, in 1886-1888. (हेनरिक हर्ट्ज़ — रेडियो तरंगों की खोज)

 

• His experiments demonstrated that electromagnetic waves could travel through air and behave like light (reflection, refraction, and polarisation), confirming Maxwell's prediction that light itself is an electromagnetic wave.

 

• The unit of frequency, the Hertz (Hz), is named in his honour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• James Clerk Maxwell formulated the classical theory of electromagnetism (Maxwell's equations) in the 1860s, unifying electricity, magnetism and light.

 

• Guglielmo Marconi later built on Hertz's work to develop practical long-distance wireless telegraphy/radio communication in the 1890s-1900s.

 

NOTE

 

• Guglielmo Marconi (Option 1): Pioneered practical, long-distance wireless communication, but this was after Hertz's foundational 1886 experiments.

 

• William Hopkins (Option 2): A 19th-century English mathematician and geologist, not connected to the discovery of radio waves.

 

• Michael Faraday (Option 3): Discovered electromagnetic induction, laying groundwork that Maxwell later mathematically formalised, but did not discover radio waves.

question: Who was the first Indian wrestler to win a world championship medal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Udey Chand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Udey Chand became the first Indian wrestler to win a medal at the World Wrestling Championships, winning a bronze medal at the 1954 World Wrestling Championships held in Tokyo, Japan. (उदय चंद — पहला विश्व कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप पदक)

 

• He was a decorated Indian Army officer and freestyle wrestler, and was honoured with the Arjuna Award for his contribution to wrestling.

 

• His achievement predates India's other major individual wrestling medals and marked the country's first breakthrough at the world championship level (as distinct from the Olympics).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first wrestling medal at the Olympic Games was won by K.D. Jadhav, who claimed bronze at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics — India's first individual Olympic medal after independence.

 

• Sushil Kumar later became the first Indian wrestler to win a World Championship gold medal, in 2010.

 

NOTE

 

• Dara Singh (Option 2): A legendary Indian professional wrestler and actor, famous for winning the Commonwealth Wrestling Championship (1959), not the World Championship.

 

• Malwa Singh (Option 3): Not associated with a world wrestling championship medal.

 

• KD Jadhav (Option 4): Won India's first individual Olympic bronze medal (1952), not a World Championship medal.

question:
Calculate personal income (in ₹ crore) from the given data.

Particulars | ₹ (in crore)

Private income | 1800

Net retained earnings of private enterprises | 500

Corporation tax | 250
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Personal Income is derived from Private Income by removing the portion of corporate profit that never reaches households — i.e. the part retained by companies and the part paid away as corporate tax. (व्यक्तिगत आय — निजी आय से गणना)

 

• The standard formula is: Personal Income = Private Income − Corporation Tax − Net Retained Earnings (Undistributed Profits) of private enterprises, since only the dividend portion of corporate profit actually accrues to households as personal income.

 

• Applying this formula: 1800 − 250 − 500 = ₹1050 crore. This does not land exactly on any of the four printed options; Option 4 (1000) is the closest listed figure to this computed value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Private Income itself is derived from National Income by adding transfer payments, interest on public debt and net factor income from abroad, and subtracting income accruing to the government/public sector.

 

• Personal Disposable Income = Personal Income − Direct personal taxes − Miscellaneous fees/fines, the next step down this income chain.

 

NOTE

 

• 950 and 1100 (Options 1 and 2): Do not match the standard formula's result as closely as Option 4.

 

• 2050 (Option 3): This is the answer marked in the source PDF's answer key; however, it does not follow from the standard Personal Income formula applied to the figures as printed (it appears to add rather than subtract the deductions), so it has not been used as the final answer here.

question:
Match the pair correctly:

National Waterways | Stretch

a) NW-1 | 1. Kakinada-Puducherry

b) NW-2 | 2. Kottapuram-Kollam

c) NW-3 | 3. Allahabad-Haldia

d) NW-5 | 4. Sadiya-Dhubri

| 5. Talcher-Dhamra
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-3, b-4, c-2, d–5.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Waterway 1 (NW-1) runs on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Allahabad (Prayagraj) to Haldia, making it India's longest national waterway. (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग — गंगा नदी प्रणाली)

 

• National Waterway 2 (NW-2) runs on the Brahmaputra river from Sadiya to Dhubri in Assam.

 

• National Waterway 3 (NW-3), the West Coast Canal, runs from Kottapuram to Kollam in Kerala, along with the Champakara and Udyogmandal canals.

 

• National Waterway 5 (NW-5) covers the Brahmani-Kharsua-Dhamra river system and the East Coast Canal, from Talcher to Dhamra in Odisha.

 

• This gives the correct matching: a-3 (NW-1: Allahabad-Haldia), b-4 (NW-2: Sadiya-Dhubri), c-2 (NW-3: Kottapuram-Kollam), d-5 (NW-5: Talcher-Dhamra).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The stretch Kakinada-Puducherry (via the canals along the east coast) corresponds to National Waterway 4 (NW-4), which is not part of this matching set.

 

• India currently has 111 National Waterways declared under the National Waterways Act, 2016, though only a handful are operational for significant cargo/passenger movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 all pair at least one waterway with the wrong stretch (e.g., assigning the NW-4 stretch of Kakinada-Puducherry to NW-1, NW-2 or NW-3), making them incorrect.

question: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 received the assent of the President on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 19 December 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 received the assent of the President of India on 19 December 2022, and was notified as Act No. 18 of 2022. (वन्यजीव संरक्षण संशोधन अधिनियम — 19 दिसंबर 2022)

 

• It amended the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972, and among other changes, implemented obligations under CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species), rationalised the schedules of protected species from six to four, and empowered the central government to regulate/prohibit the trade of exotic live species.

 

• The Act also enhanced penalties for wildlife offences and introduced provisions for the management of India's Protected Areas network.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is the principal law providing a framework for the protection of wild animals, birds and plants, and for the establishment of National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries and Tiger Reserves in India.

 

• The Act's schedules were reduced from six to four, with a new schedule specifically for species listed under CITES appendices.

 

NOTE

 

• 14, 17 and 10 December 2022 (Options 2, 3 and 4): These are close but incorrect dates; the officially notified date of presidential assent is 19 December 2022.

question: Which Excel feature allows you to simultaneously edit the same cell or range of cells with multiple users in real-time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is co-authoring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Co-authoring in Microsoft Excel (available for files stored on OneDrive/SharePoint via Microsoft 365) allows multiple users to open and edit the same workbook simultaneously in real time, with changes visible to all collaborators as they happen. (सह-लेखन — रीयल-टाइम में साझा संपादन)

 

• Each collaborating user's edits and cursor position are shown live, and the workbook auto-saves changes so everyone works on the latest version.

 

• Co-authoring works across Excel desktop, Excel for the web, and Excel mobile apps when a file is shared from a cloud location.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Co-authoring is part of Microsoft's broader Office 365 real-time collaboration suite, also available in Word and PowerPoint.

 

• Version history, another Microsoft 365 cloud feature, lets users view and restore earlier saved versions of a co-authored workbook.

 

NOTE

 

• Data Validation (Option 2): Restricts the type/range of data that can be entered into a cell; unrelated to simultaneous multi-user editing.

 

• Conditional Formatting (Option 3): Automatically formats cells based on their values or rules; not a collaboration feature.

 

• Track Changes (Option 4): Records edits made to a workbook for later review/approval, but does not allow simultaneous real-time multi-user editing of the same cells.

question: Which statement about Syama Sastri is correct?
option_2: His famous composition is Pancharatna Kritis.
option_3: He is one among the trinity of Carnatic Music.
option_4: A crater on planet mercury is named after him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He is one among the trinity of Carnatic Music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Syama Sastri (1762-1827) is one of the "Trinity of Carnatic Music", along with Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar, all born in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu. (कर्नाटक संगीत त्रयी — श्यामा शास्त्री)

 

• He was renowned for his compositions in praise of Goddess Shakti/Devi, particularly his Swarajatis dedicated to the Goddess of Madurai and Kamakshi of Kanchipuram, and for his mastery of complex talas.

 

• He was a contemporary of Tyagaraja and Dikshitar, and all three composed largely in the late 18th and early 19th centuries, shaping the classical Carnatic music tradition as it is known today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tyagaraja is known for devotional compositions to Lord Rama, and Muthuswami Dikshitar is known for compositions rich in Sanskrit and his signature (mudra) "Guruguha".

 

• The Carnatic Music Trinity's compositions form the core repertoire of South Indian classical (Carnatic) music performances even today.

 

NOTE

 

• His signature name was Guruguha (Option 1): This is the composer's signature (mudra) used by Muthuswami Dikshitar, not Syama Sastri.

 

• His famous composition is Pancharatna Kritis (Option 2): The "Pancharatna Kritis" (five gems) were composed by Tyagaraja, not Syama Sastri.

 

• A crater on planet mercury is named after him (Option 4): Mercury's craters named after Carnatic composers honour Tyagaraja (a prominent crater with the planet's "hollows" nearby), not specifically Syama Sastri.

question: Article 15 of the Constitution of India entails:
option_2: equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment
option_4: prohibition of discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
solution_text:
The correct answer is prohibition of discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 15 of the Indian Constitution, under the Right to Equality, prohibits the State from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth, or any of them. (अनुच्छेद 15 — भेदभाव का निषेध)

 

• It also empowers the State to make special provisions for women, children, and for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes, SCs and STs (Articles 15(3), 15(4) and 15(5)), and, since the 2019 amendment, for economically weaker sections (Article 15(6)).

 

• Article 15 ensures citizens have equal access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, places of public entertainment, and the use of wells, tanks, bathing ghats, roads and places of public resort maintained by the State.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Articles 14 to 18 together constitute the Right to Equality in the Indian Constitution.

 

• Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all persons (not just citizens).

 

NOTE

 

• Cultural and educational rights (Option 1): Covered under Articles 29-30, not Article 15.

 

• Equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment (Option 2): This is the subject of Article 16.

 

• Freedom of speech and expression (Option 3): This is guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a), part of the Right to Freedom, not Article 15.

question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khilafat Movement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was launched by Indian Muslims, led by the Ali Brothers (Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali) along with Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, to pressure the British government to preserve the authority of the Ottoman Caliph (Khalifa) after World War I. (खिलाफत आंदोलन — अली बंधु)

 

• The movement was significant for uniting Hindus and Muslims in the freedom struggle, as Mahatma Gandhi supported it and linked it with the Non-Cooperation Movement to build wider anti-British solidarity.

 

• A Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919, and the All India Khilafat Conference was held to organise the campaign; the movement declined after Turkey itself abolished the Caliphate in 1924 under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-1922), launched by Gandhi in tandem with the Khilafat Movement, marked the first mass movement of the Indian freedom struggle under Congress leadership.

 

• The movement was called off after the Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922.

 

NOTE

 

• Wahabi Movement (Option 1): A 19th-century Islamic revivalist and anti-British movement in India inspired by Syed Ahmad Barelvi, unrelated to the Ottoman Caliphate issue.

 

• Ahmadiya Movement (Option 3): A religious reform movement founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad in Punjab in 1889, unrelated to the Khilafat cause.

 

• Faraizi Movement (Option 4): A religious reform movement among Bengal Muslims led by Haji Shariatullah, emphasising a return to core Islamic duties (*faraiz*), unconnected to the Ottoman Caliphate.

question: Which of the following food grains highly benefited from the Green Revolution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution, introduced in India in the mid-1960s under the leadership of M.S. Swaminathan and C. Subramaniam, benefited wheat the most, especially in the states of Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. (हरित क्रांति — गेहूं की उपज)

 

• It involved the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds (largely developed from Norman Borlaug's semi-dwarf wheat varieties), along with chemical fertilizers, irrigation expansion and pesticides.

 

• India's wheat production rose dramatically through the late 1960s and 1970s, transforming the country from a food-deficit nation into one that was largely self-sufficient in food grains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rice was the second major beneficiary of the Green Revolution, though the yield gains were comparatively less dramatic than for wheat, especially in the initial phase.

 

• The Green Revolution had limited impact on pulses, oilseeds and coarse cereals like millet and barley, which is why India has historically had lower productivity growth in these crops.

 

NOTE

 

• Millet (Option 1): Largely bypassed by the Green Revolution's HYV/irrigation package; often called an "orphan crop" in this context.

 

• Barley (Option 2): Not a major beneficiary; barley cultivation area/importance actually declined post-Green Revolution as wheat expanded.

 

• Maize (Option 3): Saw some yield improvement later, but nowhere near the scale of wheat's transformation during the original Green Revolution.

question: What is ‘Padam’ in Carnatic Music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A love poem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Padam is a slow-tempo, expressive musical composition in Carnatic music that generally deals with themes of love (Sringara), often expressed as devotion of a devotee (nayika) towards a deity (nayaka). (पदम — प्रेम गीत)

 

• Padams are traditionally associated with the composer Kshetrayya, and are widely used in Bharatanatyam dance recitals for their rich expressional (*abhinaya*) content.

 

• They are typically composed in Telugu or Tamil, with slow, elaborate melodic phrases that allow for detailed emotional expression in dance and vocal rendition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important compositional forms in Carnatic music include the Varnam (a technical composition used to begin concerts/dance recitals), Kriti (devotional song, the primary form used by the Trinity), and Javali (a lighter, more overtly romantic composition).

 

• Kshetrayya (17th century) is often called the "Padam composer par excellence" for his contributions to this form.

 

NOTE

 

• A patriotic poem (Option 1), a poem about courage (Option 2) and a lullaby (Option 4): None of these describes a Padam, which is specifically centred on the theme of love/devotion (Sringara Rasa).

question: Which of the following airports is being built as India’s first ‘carbon-neutral airport’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leh airport.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is developing Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Leh (Ladakh) as India's first carbon-neutral airport. (लेह हवाई अड्डा — भारत का पहला कार्बन-न्यूट्रल हवाई अड्डा)

 

• The plan relies heavily on Leh's high solar potential, with the airport moving toward meeting its energy needs through solar power and other renewable energy sources, along with energy-efficient infrastructure.

 

• Leh airport, situated at a strategic high-altitude location in Ladakh, already plays a key logistical and defence role, and its green transformation is aimed at reducing its carbon footprint given the ecologically fragile Himalayan environment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cochin International Airport (Kerala) was the world's first fully solar-powered airport, achieving this status in 2015, though it is described separately from AAI's Leh "carbon-neutral airport" initiative.

 

• The push toward carbon-neutral/green airports is part of India's broader commitments under its climate action goals, including the Airports Council International's Airport Carbon Accreditation programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Jammu airport, Kangra airport and Srinagar airport (Options 1, 2 and 3): None of these has been designated as India's first carbon-neutral airport project; that distinction belongs to Leh airport.

question: In which country do Kachin, Karen, Karenni, Chin and Mon ethnic groups belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kachin, Karen, Karenni (Kayah), Chin and Mon are among the major recognised ethnic minority groups of Myanmar (formerly Burma), each with its own distinct language, culture and, in several cases, its own designated state within the country. (जातीय समूह — म्यांमार)

 

• Myanmar officially recognises 135 ethnic groups, broadly classified into 8 major national ethnic races: Bamar (Burman), Chin, Kachin, Kayin (Karen), Kayah (Karenni), Mon, Rakhine and Shan.

 

• Several of these groups, including the Karen and Kachin, have long histories of armed ethnic conflict with the central Myanmar government/military over autonomy and rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Myanmar shares borders with India, China, Bangladesh, Laos and Thailand, and many of its ethnic minority areas lie along these border regions.

 

• The Rohingya, a distinct Muslim minority group primarily from Rakhine State, are notably not among Myanmar's officially recognised 135 ethnic groups.

 

NOTE

 

• Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal (Options 2, 3 and 4): None of these countries has Kachin, Karen, Karenni, Chin or Mon as native ethnic groups; these are specific to Myanmar.

question: In the year 2021, which of the following ministries published the amended rules related to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)?
option_3: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) notified the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Amendment Rules, 2021, which introduced significant changes to the CSR framework under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013. (कॉर्पोरेट मामलों का मंत्रालय — सीएसआर नियम)

 

• The 2021 amendments made CSR spending mandatory (with unspent amounts to be transferred to specified funds/escrow accounts), introduced impact assessment requirements for larger CSR projects, and tightened reporting/disclosure norms.

 

• CSR in India, mandated under the Companies Act, 2013, requires eligible companies (based on net worth, turnover or net profit thresholds) to spend at least 2% of average net profits of the preceding three years on CSR activities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India was the first country in the world to legally mandate CSR spending through statute (the Companies Act, 2013).

 

• Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013 lists the permissible categories of CSR activities, such as education, healthcare, environmental sustainability and rural development.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Science and Technology, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and Ministry of Home Affairs (Options 1, 3 and 4): None of these ministries administers the Companies Act or CSR rules; that responsibility lies solely with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

question: A flat ring of small, icy bodies that revolve around the sun beyond the orbit of the planet Neptune is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuiper Belt.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kuiper Belt is a flat, disc-shaped ring of small icy bodies (comprising comets, dwarf planets and other remnants from the solar system's formation) that orbit the Sun beyond the orbit of Neptune, roughly between 30 and 55 astronomical units from the Sun. (क्विपर बेल्ट — नेपच्यून की कक्षा से परे)

 

• It is named after astronomer Gerard Kuiper, and contains icy bodies made mostly of frozen methane, ammonia and water, similar in composition to comets.

 

• The dwarf planet Pluto is the largest and best-known object located within the Kuiper Belt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Oort Cloud is a much more distant, roughly spherical shell of icy objects believed to surround the solar system far beyond the Kuiper Belt, thought to be the source of long-period comets.

 

• The Asteroid Belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, and consists mainly of rocky (not icy) bodies.

 

NOTE

 

• Asteroid Belt (Option 1): Located between Mars and Jupiter, made of rocky material, not beyond Neptune.

 

• Bow Shock (Option 2): The boundary where the Sun's solar wind meets the interstellar medium, not a ring of icy bodies.

 

• Oort Cloud (Option 4): A spherical (not flat/disc-shaped) shell of icy bodies much farther out than the Kuiper Belt.

question: In Cricket, the bowler does NOT get credit for ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is run out.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In cricket, a run out dismissal is not credited to the bowler's wicket-taking tally, because it results from a fielding effort (the batter being dismissed while attempting a run, with a fielder breaking the wicket) rather than from the bowler directly dismissing the batter. (रन आउट — गेंदबाज़ को श्रेय नहीं)

 

• Dismissals that are credited to the bowler include bowled, caught, LBW (leg before wicket), stumped, and hit wicket (in most cases).

 

• A run out can occur off any ball, including a wide or a no-ball, further underlining that it isn't dependent on the bowler's delivery in the way other dismissals are.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besides run out, the other dismissal not credited to the bowler is ‘retired out’/‘timed out’, and ‘obstructing the field’.

 

• A bowler's bowling figures (wickets) in a scorecard only include dismissals directly attributable to their delivery, as governed by the Laws of Cricket.

 

NOTE

 

• Bowled (Option 1): Credited to the bowler — the delivery directly strikes and dislodges the stumps.

 

• LBW (Option 2): Credited to the bowler — the delivery would have hit the stumps but for the batter's leg/body blocking it.

 

• Catch (Option 4): Credited to the bowler (along with the fielder who takes the catch) — the delivery induces the batter to hit the ball into a fielder's hands.

question: The Chilika Lake is located to the south of the ____________ delta.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chilika Lake, the largest brackish-water lagoon in Asia and the second largest in the world, is located in Odisha, immediately to the south of the Mahanadi river delta. (चिल्का झील — महानदी डेल्टा के दक्षिण)

 

• It is spread across the districts of Puri, Khurda and Ganjam, and connects to the Bay of Bengal through a narrow, shifting outer channel.

 

• Chilika Lake was designated the first Indian wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention, in 1981, and is a critical habitat for migratory birds, including flamingos, and the endangered Irrawaddy dolphin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahanadi River originates in Chhattisgarh and flows through Odisha before draining into the Bay of Bengal, forming a large delta near Cuttack/Paradip.

 

• Chilika's Nalabana Island, located within the lake, is a designated bird sanctuary.

 

NOTE

 

• Narmada (Option 1): Flows through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, and drains into the Arabian Sea via an estuary, not a delta near Chilika.

 

• Cauvery (Option 2): Forms a delta in Tamil Nadu, on India's south-eastern coast, unrelated to Chilika Lake.

 

• Godavari (Option 4): Forms a delta in Andhra Pradesh, further south along the east coast from Chilika, not adjacent to it.

question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam ("Dance of the Enchantress") is one of the eight recognised classical dance forms of India, originating from and traditionally performed in the state of Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• It is characterised by graceful, swaying body movements, subtle facial expressions (*abhinaya*), and is traditionally performed as a solo dance by women, often depicting the theme of *Mohini*, the enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu.

 

• The dance draws on both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali traditions of Kerala, and gained renewed prominence and standardisation in the 20th century, notably through the efforts of poet Vallathol Narayana Menon and the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala is also home to the classical dance-drama form Kathakali, distinguished by its elaborate makeup, costumes and codified hand gestures (*mudras*).

 

• The eight classical dances of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi are: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Hojagiri, not a classical dance form.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Home to the classical dance form Sattriya, not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Home to the classical dance form Bharatanatyam, not Mohiniyattam.

question: In which year was the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) was formed in December 1928, as the governing body for cricket in India. (भारतीय क्रिकेट नियंत्रण बोर्ड — 1928)

 

• It is registered as a society under the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, with its headquarters at the Cricket Centre, Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai.

 

• BCCI became a full member of the International Cricket Council (ICC) and is today the richest cricket board in the world, administering domestic tournaments like the Ranji Trophy and the Indian Premier League (IPL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India played its first official Test match in 1932, against England at Lord's, a few years after BCCI's formation.

 

• The first President of BCCI was R.E. Grant Govan, and the first secretary was Anthony De Mello.

 

NOTE

 

• 1914 (Option 1): Predates the formation of BCCI; around this period, cricket in India was organised more informally through regional associations.

 

• 1931 (Option 2): Not the year BCCI was established.

 

• 1947 (Option 3): The year of India's independence, unrelated to BCCI's founding, which occurred nearly two decades earlier.
